title: Synthetic customer-environment fidelity runner with regression detection
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: build a portable, reproducible runner that synthesizes a customer's VPC/on-prem environment and exercises the inference runtime end-to-end to measure tokens/sec, p95 latency, and detect regressions. This runner is intended for Private/VPC/on-prem validation runs and pre-upgrade checks to ensure changes to the serving runtime or kernel selection do not degrade performance or tail latency.

Scope: the first iteration will support: deterministic traffic generation (request pacing and KV-cache priming), topology seeding (simple service dependency emulation), containerized scenario driver that can run inside a mirrored VPC or on a local on-prem sandbox, metric collection compatible with telemetry pipeline (prometheus-compatible counters and histograms), and an automated regression detector that posts alerts to Slack and creates tickets when thresholds are exceeded.

Success metrics: baseline runs reproduce tokens/sec within +/-5% of recorded customer runs, p95 latency within +/-10% versus snapshot baseline, and regression detector false positive rate < 6% on historical runs.
acceptance_criteria: Runnable CLI + container image that accepts an environment snapshot and prompt set and returns a structured run report (JSON)
Metrics exported as Prometheus metrics and a summarized run report including tokens/sec, p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, error rates, and KV-cache hit curves

Regression detector that compares current run to baseline and triggers a Slack alert and creates a Linear ticket when: tokens/sec decreases by >5% (relative) OR p95 increases by >10% (relative) OR API error rate increases >0.5% absolute
Repro runs are repeatable: running the same snapshot + seed prompts 3x produces metrics with CV < 3% for tokens/sec
Runbook and playbook exist for interpreting results and triage steps for infra/serving/runtime teams
design_notes: We will use a deterministic token pacing strategy that replays request inter-arrival times sampled from the customer's distribution but deterministic-seeded to allow repeatability.
KV-cache priming sequences are configurable per-model and will be included as a preamble pass to warm caches to baseline steady-state throughput measurements.
Use protobuf-encoded trace blobs to keep run artifacts compact; JSON summaries are generated for dashboards and tickets.

Decision: implement the driver in Go for lightweight concurrency and lower resource overhead vs k6. k6 was considered but lacks easy deterministic seeding for token-level pacing and KV-cache priming logic.
Storage/traces: prefer S3-compatible object store in customer mirror for persistence; fall back to ephemeral local storage when running in constrained on-prem sandboxes.
Tracing format will include model variant, quantization profile, sequence length histogram, and kernel selection hints to aid root cause analysis of regressions.
tradeoffs_and_open_questions: Proto vs JSON: protobuf reduces size (important for long histories) but adds serialization maintenance overhead for test fixtures.
Alert thresholds are currently heuristic (5% tokens/sec, 10% p95). We should run historical calibration across 20 customer snapshots before finalizing thresholds.
How to handle variable system-level load on customer sandboxes — plan: include a co-located system load probe and require min available CPU/GPU util thresholds for the run to be considered valid.
Privacy: we will avoid storing PII; input prompt sets must be sanitized and optionally replaced with synthetic equivalents when customers require it.
implementation_plan: Week 1: prototype deterministic generator + proto summary format; basic prometheus metrics export
Week 2: add KV-cache priming, implement seedable workload runner, build container image and simple CLI
Week 3: integrate regression detector and Slack ticket creation; wire up to CI to run baseline nightly for internal fixtures
Week 4: run against 5 opt-in customer snapshots to calibrate detection thresholds and collect variance statistics
Week 5: finalize runbook, security review, and ship runtime-1.20 validation job template
test_plan: Unit tests for pacing logic and cache-priming sequences
Integration test that runs containerized scenario against a minimal on-prem sandbox and validates metric exports
Stress test that ramps to target tokens/sec for sustained 30m to validate autoscaling signals and batching behavior
Regression test harness that re-runs historical customer snapshot and verifies detector does not fire on known-good runs
metrics_and_signals: Latency histograms: p50/p90/p95/p99 request latency (model + network)
KV-cache hit ratio over time and warmup curve
System: GPU util, GPU memory, CPU steal, network bandwidth to storage
regression_detection_details: Detector runs a two-sided comparison of current run vs baseline using trimmed-mean and EWMA to reduce sensitivity to outliers
Triggers when relative tokens/sec drop > 5% with p-value < 0.05 across replicated runs, OR when p95 latency increases by >10% relative with supporting increase in p99
Secondary checks correlate with kernel selection changes or quantization profile differences; if kernel differences present, detector lowers severity and annotates ticket for manual triage
Detector creates ticket template with links to run artifacts, diffed histograms, and suggested next owners (runtime/compilers/infra)
All thresholds are configurable per-customer via scenario YAML
runbook_and_playbook: How to interpret a tokens/sec regression: check KV-cache warmup curves first, then model variant and quantization profile, then kernel selection logs
If p95 regression with unchanged tokens/sec: investigate queueing/backpressure or GC spikes on the runtime host
If errors spike: collect application logs, core dumps, and perf profiles and attach to ticket
Escalation path: runtime-oncall -> infra-oncall -> compilers team depending on annotation in regression detector ticket
